source_title: Odisha eyes semiconductor push with five projects worth over $4 billion - Business Standard
source_excerpt: Odisha has lined up semiconductor projects with proposed investments of around $4.7 billion as the state steps up efforts to establish a foothold in the global chip manufacturing and advanced electronics value chain. The projects, which include semiconductor fabrication and advanced 3D chip packaging, are expected to mark a significant shift in Odisha's industrial landscape, traditionally dominated by mining, metals and mineral-based industries. Vishal Kumar Dev, additional chief secretary of the Electronics and Information Technology Department, said the state has so far approved five projects worth over $1.2 billion and two of the 12 projects approved under the India Semiconductor Mission are coming up in Odisha. "We have a pipeline of semiconductor projects worth over $4 billion. India's first compound semiconductor fabrication unit and the first advanced 3D chip packaging unit are being built in the state at speed with the groundbreaking conducted within six to eight months of the approval," he said at TiECon Bhubaneswar 2026. Among the projects moving towards operationalisation is the Rs 618 crore semiconductor facility of RIR Power Electronics Ltd at the Electronic Manufacturing Cluster in Info Valley-II near Bhubaneswar. This is the country's first vertically integrated silicon carbide semiconductor manufacturing facility, which is expected to begin commercial production shortly. The company has already installed specialised silicon carbide epitaxial wafer manufacturing reactors at the facility. All physical infrastructure and installation of key equipment, including the reactors required for manufacturing SiC epitaxial wafers, have been completed. Essential power connections, utilities and supporting infrastructure have also been commissioned, bringing the facility close to commercial operations. "The facility is likely to be inaugurated later this month or early next month," said a company executive. The company expects to initially manufacture around 750 SiC epitaxial wafers by the end of the year, with production targeted to increase to 20,000 wafers by the end of 2027. Silicon carbide is a wide-bandgap semiconductor material that offers advantages over conventional silicon, particularly in high-voltage, high-temperature and high-power applications. SiC-based devices are high in demand for electric vehicles, renewable energy systems, industrial power electronics, strategic sectors such as defence and aerospace, where energy efficiency and performance are critical. The five semiconductor projects in Odisha also include the Rs 3,406-crore SiC semiconductor facility of SiCSem Private Limited, which has secured the necessary approvals for its proposed manufacturing unit. The project is expected to manufacture silicon carbide diodes and MOSFETs. Another major investment is being made by US-headquartered 3D Glass Solutions (3DGS), which has proposed an integrated advanced packaging and embedded glass substrate manufacturing facility with an investment of Rs 1,943 crore. The company has partnered with Intel Corporation for the country's first advanced 3D chip packaging facility, with glass-core technology expected to play an important role in next-generation semiconductor packaging. The other two projects are being developed by ASP Semicon Private Limited and Sancode Semi Private Limited. ASP Semicon is setting up a semiconductor memory chip modules manufacturing facility in Khordha with an investment of Rs 4,620 crore, while Sancode Semi plans to establish an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) facility at Info Valley-II with an investment of Rs 1,650 crore. Dev said advanced packaging would be a critical area of opportunity for the state, particularly as semiconductor manufacturers increasingly look beyond conventional chip fabrication to develop more sophisticated packaging technologies that improve performance, efficiency and integration. "Advanced chip packaging is the next step and Odisha is taking an edge, among others, in pivoting towards advanced packaging units, especially in glass-core technology. Our collaboration with global companies like Intel and 3D Glass Solutions intends to take the lead in the global semiconductor value chain," he said. The state's semiconductor push is being complemented by investments in AI infrastructure and digital technologies. Odisha has announced an AI policy and an Odisha AI Mission, while work is progressing on a proposed sovereign AI hub aimed at building domestic computing capabilities and supporting the deployment of artificial intelligence across sectors. "Today, data is the new oil, but tomorrow, compute will be the new oil and Odisha has taken a leap forward here as well. Odisha is leading India's AI transformation by announcing an Odisha AI Mission, work under which is progressing at a very rapid pace. It is also building a first-of-its-kind sovereign AI hub to become India's digital and compute bank. Here, AI will be used by Odisha, for Odisha and in Odisha," Dev added.
